Hi Samir — thanks, good questions. Below is a concise summary you can share with LegalOps; I also copied our Ops and Compliance leads to confirm details. TL;DR: replicated DR snapshots are subject to the same deletion intent but there are operational windows and tombstone workflows that affect timing.

1) Geo-replicated DR snapshots: when an account deletion/erasure request is accepted, we mark the primary data for erasure immediately and kick off a deletion job for associated backups. For replicated DR snapshots in other regions (e.g., US copies of EU customer snapshots), those snapshots are tombstoned and moved to a deletion queue. Physical deletion occurs during the next regional retention sweep. Typical timeline: tombstone applied within minutes; physical removal depends on the sweep cadence (configurable, default 14 days). If expedited deletion is requested, we can trigger a manual sweep (subject to product/ops approval).

2) Restore window and authorization: after tombstone, snapshots remain recoverable until physically deleted. The default recoverability window equals the configured sweep window (so by default ~14 days). Restores from DR copies require dual-approval: a request from the account owner or support case, plus an Ops engineer to execute (we log all actions). For EU-resident deletion requests where the customer requires irreversibility, we recommend the expedited sweep process and locking the restore capability (see #3).

3) Legal holds: if a legal hold is applied before deletion, we transition snapshots to a quarantine hold state. Quarantined snapshots are excluded from scheduled deletion/sweep workflows until the hold is released. During this time restores are restricted to authorized legal/ops personnel only and are audited. If LegalOps requires, we can add a policy that quarantined snapshots are moved to a hardened storage class and flagged in the retention index.

I'll let Laura and Hannah add exact timing and ops playbook steps (manual sweep SLA, audit entries, and how we document the expedited deletion). If you want me to produce a one-page summary for your legal team I can do that and include the manual-sweep request template.

Samir / team — adding operational specifics from the DR/Snapshot side. I attached a small diagram showing cross-region flow (eu-dataflow-diagram.png).

- Tombstone vs physical deletion: when tombstoned we retain metadata (owner, retention policies, tombstone timestamp) but the data is scheduled for physical purge. Our default background sweep runs once every 14 days at the region level. That means maximum exposure after tombstone is 14 days, but in practice most items are purged in the first sweep after tombstone.

- Expedited purge: for GDPR-right-to-erasure requests where the customer insists on immediate physical deletion we follow a documented manual purge playbook. This includes:
  * Submit manual purge ticket (internal form + link)
  * Ops triage to validate no active legal hold or compliance exception
  * Execute expedited region-local purge (we do not cross-region replicate the physical delete action; we apply it to the target region snapshots)
  * Post-purge verification and Audit log export (signed off by Ops mgr)

- Cross-region nuance: if the primary dataset is EU and DR replicas are in US, the manual purge will remove the US replica as part of the purge run. However, because of cross-region replication latency and the index update cycle, there is a small window (minutes to a couple hours) where a restore job might still find the replica before the purge completes. That window is why we recommend coordinated manual purge + disabling restore capability for the account during the operation.

- Auditability: every tombstone/purge/restore action produces an immutable audit record with timestamp, operator, and job-id (we attach these to the customer incident record). We can produce a signed attestation for LegalOps that includes the job-ids and timestamps.

I can attach the standard manual-purge request template (I included it in the Drive link).

Samir — quick operational confirmation from Compliance:

1) Policy enforcement: Our deletion policy requires we respect regulatory requests. For EU residents we default to the expedited purge path when flagged by LegalOps.

2) Legal hold interplay: holds always win. If LegalOps places a hold, no purge action will run until LegalOps clears it. We do, however, quarantine the artifact and mark it as non-recoverable by normal support workflows — only Compliance-approved restores are permitted.

If LegalOps wants a hold instead, reply with hold scope (full account / specific snapshot ids) and expected hold duration.

I'll loop in the audit team after you confirm so we can prepare the attestation package.
